_comment: Hand-maintained test matrix. Maps each renderer/client to your real-world test status. Edit freely, then rerun: python scripts/gen_compatibility.py. Status is shown verbatim; use 'Tested', 'Partial', or 'Not yet tested'.

esp32_bin.hardware: Waveshare 13.3" Spectra 6 (ESP32-S3-WROOM-2) + Waveshare 7.3" PhotoPainter (ESP32-S3) + Seeed reTerminal E1002 and E1004 (Spectra 6) + Seeed XIAO 13.3" ePaper EE02 (Spectra 6) + Waveshare 10.85" e-Paper HAT+ (G) BWRY on an ESP32-S3 Zero via tesserae-device-firmware + paperlesspaper OpenPaper 7 (ESP32-C6, 7.3" Spectra 6 picture frame) via tesserae-device-firmware
esp32_bin.notes: Primary daily driver, battery-powered, deep-sleep. The 13.3" client lives at tesserae-device-esp32-bin; the 7.3" PhotoPainter client at tesserae-device-photopainter-7.3-bin. Both pair with the same renderer; the panel preset (waveshare_e6_13_3 vs waveshare_photopainter_7_3) selects the firmware-native row stride. The reTerminal Spectra 6 SKUs consume the same 4-bpp packed frames through tesserae-device-firmware.

esp32_gray_bin.hardware: Seeed reTerminal E1003 (10.3" 1872x1404, 16-level grayscale) running tesserae-device-firmware; also the original M5Stack M5Paper (4.7" 960x540 via an IT8951 controller, classic ESP32-D0WDQ6-V3) running tesserae-device-firmware, plus the Seeed XIAO ePaper EE03 (same 10.3" panel on the XIAO driver board) and the M5Stack PaperS3 (4.7" 960x540, raw parallel glass), both not yet tested + reMarkable 2 (10.3" 1404x1872, 16-level greyscale) via the community tesserae.remarkable AppLoad app
esp32_gray_bin.notes: Confirmed end-to-end on the bench, including GT911 touch input round-tripping through the tap pipeline. The 4-bpp nibble-packed frame (1314144 bytes) is fetched over REST and painted with no on-device decode. The original M5Paper is also confirmed end-to-end (2026-09-10): the same it8951_gray driver on classic-ESP32 silicon at the PaperS3's 960x540 geometry, plus battery telemetry, the three side buttons, the SHT30 sensor and GT911 touch. Touch reports in the 540x960 composition space and needs the panel kept awake -- the classic ESP32 cannot wake from deep sleep on the touch INT. The EE03 paints a byte-identical frame to the E1003 (same ED103TC2 glass behind the same IT8951 controller); the PaperS3 shares this renderer at a different geometry. Those two are awaiting a first bring-up on real hardware.

pi_bin.notes: Fastest Pi path, packed buffer written straight to inky's _buf.

pi_png.notes: Works on every inky-supported panel; quantises on the Pi each frame.

esp32_bw_bin.hardware: Xteink X4 (GDEQ0426T82 / SSD1677, 800x480 mono) running CrossInk with Tesserae client support + Seeed reTerminal E1001 (800x480 mono) running tesserae-device-firmware
esp32_bw_bin.notes: 1-bpp packing confirmed end-to-end: a 48000-byte frame fetched and painted on the panel with no on-device decode, upright in the portrait_flipped composition. The X4 is an e-reader, so the dashboard is its sleep screen rather than a wake-cycle refresh. The remaining Seeed 800x480 mono SKUs (XIAO ePaper 7.5", EE04 7.5") and the Waveshare 4.2" share this renderer but are still unconfirmed.

trmnl_png.hardware: Amazon Kindle Paperwhite 2 (jailbroken) via KOReader trmnl-display plugin + Seeed TRMNL 7.5" OG DIY Kit (XIAO 7.5" panel running the TRMNL firmware) + TRMNL X (stock firmware, 1872x1404)
trmnl_png.notes: 1-bit greyscale PNG fitted to the panel + dithered server-side.

esp32_gray2_bin.hardware: Xteink X4 (SSD1677, 800x480) and Xteink X3 (UC8279d, 792x528), both running CrossInk with Tesserae client support + Seeed reTerminal E1001 (4-gray mode) running tesserae-device-firmware + Seeed reTerminal Sticky (SSD1677, 480x800 portrait) running tesserae-device-firmware + M5Stack PaperMono (SSD1677, 480x800 portrait) running tesserae-device-firmware, not yet tested
esp32_gray2_bin.notes: 4-level grayscale confirmed end-to-end: the 2-bpp frame is fetched and composited as a base frame plus LSB/MSB planes, with distinct grey levels. Packing is byte-identical to the firmware's own 2-bpp bitmap reader, so no decode step is involved. Notable that this works on the X3's UC8253/UC8279d silicon as well as the UC8179-class panels the renderer was written for. The Sticky packs the same 96000 bytes at a portrait 120-byte stride because its firmware transposes on the device; only the stride distinguishes it from the E1001. The PaperMono is the Sticky's controller family on M5Stack's board and packs the same portrait stride; its firmware target was built from the published pin map and awaits a first bring-up on real hardware.

circuitpython_bmp.hardware: Raspberry Pi 3 + Waveshare 7" 1024x600 HDMI touch display, and Raspberry Pi 5 + Pi Touch Display 2 (10.1"), both running the community CircuitPython client under PyGame
circuitpython_bmp.notes: Confirmed on Pi-class hardware via the displayio PyGame emulation, pairing through the v1 REST discover flow as circuitpython_generic and painting the uncompressed indexed BMP with no zlib step. Held short of Tested because the microcontroller path the renderer was written for (Pico W class boards decoding via adafruit_imageload) is still unverified. Client: https://github.com/bablokb/tesserae-device-circuitpython
